# Connecting the Dots

> Independent research atlas by Robert Bregy about Internet TLDs, ICANN applications, governance, economics and society. Available in English, Italian, German and French.

Website version 0.7.108, published 2026-11-10. This is the technical/editorial release date, not the observation date of every fact. Read the source date and scope beside each claim.

## Start here

- [Machine-readable catalog](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/agent-catalog.json): page URLs, data units, source dates, provenance, licensing and archived releases.
- [Reading-page index](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/discovery/manifest.json): focused HTML pages and their available Markdown versions, in all four languages.
- [Research and citation](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/research/): method, current working paper, archived evidence and how to cite it.
- [Complete data manifest](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/manifest.json): existing CSV/JSON resources and integrity information.

## Reading pages

- [Economic cases | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/economics/en/cases/index.md): Eight documented cases show how renewals, auctions, acquisitions, regulation and public revenue create value in the domain economy.
- [TLD adoption and shares | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/economics/en/market/index.md): Compare TLD website presence and registered-domain counts with filters, dates, sources and downloadable data.
- [Portfolios and contention | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/economics/en/portfolios/index.md): Portfolios, multiple applications and contention: compare operator strategies and selected cases from the ICANN 2026 round.
- [The economics of the 2026 round | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/economics/en/round-2026/index.md): Application costs, string themes, applicant activity and economic strategies in the ICANN 2026 round.
- [Is a domain only there to find a website? | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/guides/en/beyond/index.md): From services we use to the invisible functions of DNS, then writing systems and alternative naming systems.
- [What is a city's own domain for? | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/guides/en/cities/index.md): Start with governance models and cases. Ask how to measure usefulness, then compare different generations of projects.
- [Who creates value, and who collects it? | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/guides/en/economics/index.md): Follow the money through the domain market, from registration payments to the strategies of extension operators.
- [How does an Internet name work? | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/guides/en/how/index.md): First the address and the actors, then the lifecycle, economics and rules. The glossary is always within reach.
- [What might .lugano become? | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/guides/en/lugano/index.md): Start with the application's status and the author's position. Then read intentions, open decisions, possible uses and verification criteria.
- [How have Internet names changed? | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/guides/en/timeline/index.md): Follow the history, compare application rounds and then examine the classifications and their limitations.
- [.ai: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/ai/index.md): Anguilla’s country code. Its association with artificial intelligence illustrates how an existing name can acquire a new meaning.
- [.amazon: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/amazon/index.md): At the documented check, .amazon was delegated in the DNS root as Generic. Explore its dated status, history and IANA/ICANN sources in this Connecting the Dots profile.
- [.berlin: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/berlin/index.md): At the documented check, .berlin was delegated in the DNS root as Generic. Explore its dated status, history and IANA/ICANN sources in this Connecting the Dots profile.
- [.cat: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/cat/index.md): A name for the Catalan linguistic and cultural community: a belonging that crosses state borders.
- [.com: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/com/index.md): Created for commercial activities before the Web. It later became a symbol of online presence.
- [.io: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/io/index.md): At the documented check, .io was delegated in the DNS root as Country-code. Explore its dated status, history and IANA/ICANN sources in this Connecting the Dots profile.
- [.lugano: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/lugano/index.md): An application by the City of Lugano in the 2026 round. It is not yet operational: approval, delegation and future uses remain to be established.
- [.music: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/music/index.md): At the documented check, .music was delegated in the DNS root as Generic. Explore its dated status, history and IANA/ICANN sources in this Connecting the Dots profile.
- [.swiss: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/swiss/index.md): At the documented check, .swiss was delegated in the DNS root as Generic. Explore its dated status, history and IANA/ICANN sources in this Connecting the Dots profile.
- [.zuerich: history, status and sources | Connecting the Dots](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/tlds/en/zuerich/index.md): At the documented check, .zuerich was delegated in the DNS root as Generic. Explore its dated status, history and IANA/ICANN sources in this Connecting the Dots profile.

## Data and scope

The combined Explorer contains 2,788 names: 1,849 base records plus 980 frozen 2026 primary strings, minus 41 overlapping names. This is not a count of delegated TLDs. The root snapshot contains 1,437 TLDs at 2026-10-04.

The APS export observed at 2026-10-11T21:27:40.214Z contains 2,783 rows: 1,614 base applications and 1,169 linked replacement rows. Its new-primary subset has 1,608 applications over 980 strings; 6 other base applications concern variants of existing TLDs. The separately published official total is 1,615; retain the documented public-listing gap.

- [TLD and historical profile universe](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/tld_universe.csv): 1,599 records; unit: TLD/profile identity. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/iana_snapshot.json).
- [Base Explorer catalog](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/explorer_catalog.csv): 1,849 records; unit: distinct name. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/manifest.json).
- [Frozen secondary Reveal Day primary-string inventory](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/applications_2026_strings_reveal.csv): 980 records; unit: distinct new primary string. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/application_2026_snapshot.json).
- [ICANN APS public listing, original fields preserved](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/applications_2026_aps_official_listing.csv): 2,783 records; unit: APS listing row. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/applications_2026_aps_official_provenance.json).
- [Published APS applications and their string relationships](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/aps_2026_application_graph.json): 1,614 records; unit: published base application. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/aps_2026_application_graph_manifest.json).
- [Source-dated APS status observations](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/aps_2026_record_observations.csv): 2,783 records; unit: source observation of an APS record. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/aps_2026_application_graph_manifest.json).
- [Separately curated local 2026 application records](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/applications_2026.csv): 1 records; unit: locally curated application record. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/application_2026_snapshot.json).
- [APS snapshot analysis · 11 October 2026](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/aps_2026_current_analytics.csv): 1,614 records; unit: published base application with explicit analysis scopes. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/aps_2026_current_analytics_manifest.json).
- [Historical ICANN 2012 application–string–applicant graph](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/applications_2012.csv): 1,930 records; unit: 2012 application. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/application_archaeology_manifest.json).
- [Source-backed economic metrics](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/economic_metrics.csv): 22 records; unit: economic observation. [Provenance](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/manifest.json).

## Interpretation and citation

Application, delegation, replacement, variant and derived exact-string grouping have different meanings. A false APS contention flag does not establish absence of contention before String Evaluation. Facts, interpretation and prospective ideas remain separate; undocumented outcomes are not inferred.

The current archived research release is [RR2](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23288603), bibliographic publication date 2026-10-11, evidence cutoff 2026-10-10. The newer website and the APS snapshot analysis acquired on 11 October 2026 are not automatically included in this DOI. Previous research releases remain immutable and separately citable.

- [Citation file](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/CITATION.cff): archived research citation.
- [Research release manifest](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/research/research_release_manifest.json): archived versions and working-paper relationship.
- [Bibliographic date clarification](https://robertbregy.github.io/Connecting-the-Dots/data/research_bibliographic_corrections.json): deposit creation, GitHub release, evidence cutoff and Zenodo publication date.
